name: Tine Ghealáin

attributes.attribute: the light over the fen at night
a light held by a dead gambler

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tine Ghealán is the Irish name for the light over a fen at night. The folk said it was a lantern held by a dead gambler. His soul was too dark for heaven, so he won his way back by beating the devil at cards. His name was later given to the hollow turn kept at Samain.

okr.objective: Set down Tine Ghealán as the fen light of Irish folk tale.
key_results: Names the fen a light at night
States it was held by a dead gambler
